title: Cyber Canvas
blurb: Glowing nodes, fading connection lines, and mouse parallax drift on a near-black background.
technique:
The effect places **N** particle nodes (scaled with viewport area, capped at 120) on a `<canvas>` element. Each node is assigned a random drift angle and speed; a `depth` value (0.3–1.0) controls its parallax response. Positions wrap at canvas edges with a small gutter so the field feels infinite and seamless.

Every `requestAnimationFrame` tick computes a frame `dt` by dividing elapsed milliseconds by 16.667 ms (one 60 fps tick) and capping it at 3 to prevent large jumps when the tab resumes from sleep. Node positions advance by `vx × dt` and `vy × dt`, keeping motion physically consistent across different monitor refresh rates.

**Connection lines** are drawn between every pair of nodes whose squared distance is below `CONN_DIST²` (avoiding a `sqrt` for the early-out). The `strokeStyle` alpha is set to `(1 − dist / CONN_DIST) × 0.42`, so distant pairs are nearly invisible while close pairs glow brightly in `#38bdf8`. With at most 120 nodes the O(n²) loop stays fast, touching ≤ 7 140 pairs per frame.

Mouse parallax works by exponentially smoothing (`lerp` factor 0.06 per frame) the raw `mousemove` cursor position toward the rendered position each tick. Each node's screen coordinate is then offset by `(cursor − centre) / viewport × PARALLAX_PX × depth`, so foreground nodes shift more than background ones. A faint vanishing-point perspective grid (radial ray lines plus power-law-spaced horizontal cross-lines, both at < 6% alpha) and a scanline pass (1 px black fill every 4 px at 2.8% alpha) complete the high-tech atmosphere without competing with the node network.
